# Database-free test suites that CI runs in the `static` job.
#
# jest resolves 157 suites. CI ran 92 of them (tests/unit, tests/probes,
# tests/core, __tests__/autonomy); the other 65 were never named anywhere,
# which is how they stopped running without anyone deciding they should (#7).
#
# Every suite below was verified to need no database: pointed at the same
# unroutable placeholder URL the `static` job already sets, all 31 pass, with
# 530 assertions and none skipped. That last part matters — a suite that passes
# by skipping everything spends the suite's credibility vouching for nothing.
#
# They are listed file by file rather than by directory because the directories
# are mixed. Three of the six __tests__/security suites need a real database,
# as do two of the five in tests/ai; adding the parent directory would put a
# guaranteed failure on the blocking path.
#
# To re-verify this list, or to check a suite before adding one:
#
#   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://ci:ci@127.0.0.1:1/unused \
#   TEST_DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_URL DIRECT_URL=$DATABASE_URL \
#   JWT_SECRET=ci-not-a-real-secret \
#   npx jest --runTestsByPath <path> --ci
#
# A suite that fails with PrismaClientInitializationError needs a database and
# belongs in the `autonomy` job instead, not here.

__tests__/billing/model-backed-tools-are-charged.test.ts
__tests__/integration/auth-flow.test.ts
__tests__/lib/agent-ops.test.ts
__tests__/lib/auth/middleware.test.ts
__tests__/lib/auth/rbac.test.ts
__tests__/lib/services/apiKeyUsage.test.ts
__tests__/security/admin-step-up.test.ts
__tests__/security/ai-data-access.test.ts
__tests__/security/tenant-isolation.test.ts
__tests__/suite1.basic-lifecycle.test.ts
tests/ai/brain-build-signals.test.ts
tests/ai/cross-turn-referential.test.ts
tests/ai/proposals.test.ts

tests/auth/email-eligibility.test.ts
tests/auth/email-trust.test.ts
tests/blueprints/blueprint-routing.test.ts
tests/blueprints/plan-coverage.test.ts
tests/blueprints/resume-routing.test.ts
tests/build-runs/flag.test.ts
tests/build-runtime/build-runtime.test.ts

tests/build-runtime/reliability-regression.test.ts

# Added 2026-09-04 by the suite-accounting reconciliation. These nine guard
# recently shipped work (analytics posture, free-plan resolution, email outcome
# categorisation, privacy-page integrity, the PGRST clock diagnostic and handler
# response preservation, purge safety, API-key plaintext) and were in NO
# manifest at all, so no job ran them and nothing could report them missing.
# Each was measured against the unroutable placeholder URL and PASSES with no
# database, which is what puts them here rather than in the integration job.
__tests__/analytics/amplitude-config.test.tsx
__tests__/analytics/amplitude-resilience.test.tsx
__tests__/billing/free-plan-resolution.test.ts
__tests__/email/send-outcome.test.ts
__tests__/legal/privacy-integrity.test.ts

__tests__/observability/pgrst-handler-response-preserved.test.ts
__tests__/projects/purge-safety.test.ts
__tests__/security/api-key-plaintext.test.ts

# Self-hosted runs without billing and refuses a second project (commit 3).
# Database-free on purpose: both paths short-circuit on the edition before
# touching Prisma, and asserting that they do is half the point.
__tests__/edition/single-tenant-runtime.test.ts

# The Entitlements seam: single-tenant resolves without a Plan or Subscription
# row, cloud delegates to the @cloud/* provider, and the alias stays
# overlay-first in all three configs. Database-free because proving the
# single-tenant path never reaches Prisma is the assertion itself.
__tests__/edition/entitlements-seam.test.ts

# The quota kernel enforces the numbers the seam hands it. Covers the two
# fields it used to read straight off a Plan row (apiQuotaIsLifetime and
# maxMonthlyActiveUsers) and the fail-open path. Prisma and the seam are both
# mocked, so no database.
__tests__/edition/quota-kernel-entitlements.test.ts

# REGRESSION: a self-hosted install may deploy, add a domain and create a
# trigger. The enforcement family used to read Subscription directly, so with
# no Subscription row it blocked all three while entitlements said allowed.
# Database-free because the assertion is that no Plan or Subscription row is
# ever read.
__tests__/edition/self-host-enforcement.test.ts

# The PlatformSignals seam: single-tenant reacts to nothing and never
# consults the Cloud provider, the seam absorbs provider failures rather than
# failing a signup that already succeeded, and the three signup flows report
# rather than importing the referral implementation.
__tests__/edition/platform-signals-seam.test.ts

# REGRESSION: the sandbox lifecycle primitive performs an already-authorized
# transition and no longer re-derives commercial policy. That was the SECOND
# reason a self-hosted deploy failed. Pins the deploy route ordering, because
# removing a gate is only safe if the caller really does gate.
__tests__/edition/sandbox-lifecycle.test.ts

# The lib/platform/controls split. Its public half is load-bearing: the Phase 3
# self-hosted signup slot, the operator kill switches, the security audit log
# and project lockdown all stay in OSS. Only the scoring of a stranger is
# Cloud, and the ordering (slot, switches, blocklist, then Cloud) is pinned.
__tests__/edition/platform-controls-split.test.ts

# README.md is the acceptance script for a self-hosted install, so it is checked
# against the module bootstrap renders its prerequisite guidance from. Compares
# committed text to committed code; no database.
__tests__/bootstrap/readme-matches-bootstrap.test.ts

# The documented self-host path must stay executable. Four defects found by
# running the README on a clean Ubuntu machine; the runtime half of finding 4
# lives in scripts/test/sql-file-access.sh. Reads committed text; no database.
__tests__/setup/self-host-path.test.ts
